analysis.title: US Market Intelligence - Afternoon Briefing
key_insights: SPX +2.3%, NDX +3.4%, RTY +3.1% on Nov 9 in a broad rally with about 84% of SPX members higher, rebounding from last week's sell-off. Positive US/Iran headlines on uranium enrichment levels, moving some enriched uranium, and inspections added support.

James Creager lists 10 reasons for the rebound: clean positioning, depressed sentiment, lower yields, geopolitical hopes after the midterms, oversold RSI (NDX RSI at 30), SPX P/E down about 3x since May, coming buybacks, easing AI data center worries, robust macro data, and CTAs now short equities with VIX back near 20.
High-touch volumes were at YTD and QTD lows, which the desk reads as lack of conviction in the bounce.

JPM Data Intelligence: institutional sentiment fell below -2z at the end of October and shows signs of troughing. There have been 5 comparable episodes since 2021, and markets rebounded after each, with the strongest returns typically over the following 20 days.

Brian Heavey (TMT): de-risked positioning is the main driver of the tech rally. Equity L/S net leverage is at 3-year lows and global momentum exposure is near 3-year lows. Hyperscalers and semis rallied after last Thursday's sell-off, while NVDA fell on news about CEO Jensen Huang.

Brian Heavey: flows show early signs of re-risking but volumes are down 45% vs the 5-day average. Info Tech is the largest buy sector, and much of the demand is short covering in Internet and tax-loss names.

Josh Meyers (TMT): Bloomberg reports two new GOOGL TPU variants, the 8tx and 8i Max, that are reconfigured rather than new silicon. The desk believes AVGO designed the 8i Max and is excited about the upcoming AVGO-designed Blade Runner TPU. The headline hits NVDA at an unfortunate time.

Manish Sinha (Delta-One): the AI Momentum Index has not had a clear recovery day in 10 days and fell again today. Short interest has stabilized, suggesting aggressive short covering may be behind us. Today's bounce looks driven by hedge removal and retail buying, so long buying may still need to wait.

Brendan Henrici (Energy): a basket of '26 Energy IPOs rose about 9%, the best day since July, led by FRVO +25%. Lockup-expiry shorts squeezed first, and SMRs are up 30%+ in several names. In BTM, disliked names LBRT and AESI led.

Brendan Henrici: solar is weak because rates are stabilizing higher as the data center trade recovers, and renewables became a safe haven in power after the midterms. TSLA breaking ground on a $10bn solar facility (operational 1Q29) keeps headline risk on panel makers FSLR and TE.
Democrats now hold new majorities in the House and Senate, and may hold hearings on climate policy rollbacks and try to restore renewable incentives.

Jackie Bukzin (HC): healthcare is leaning about 5x better to buy on the floor, with volumes down about 50% vs the 5-day average. ROIV is the best name, with multiple holders adding. TMO and A are better to buy, and the desk sees small shorting in TGTX. ARWR is caught up in the IONS sell-off.
Dubravko reiterates a YE26 SPX target of 8,000 on $365 EPS at 21.9x, which implies 8.4% upside from Friday's close.

Dubravko's view of the sell-off: it was a de-leveraging event. October was the largest single-month unwind for Long Momentum (about -11%, roughly 6 standard deviations), with Momentum L/S down about 40% from its peak.
Dubravko says multiples have compressed about 4x since January. AI company multiples are down about 35% since May: semis 52%, hyperscalers 14%, memory 60%, and processing units 50%.

Dubravko on how much selling is left: Momentum crowding reset from the 100th to the 76th percentile, levered ETFs sold about $60bn Thursday and $35bn the prior Friday, CTAs are net short with maybe $50bn left to sell, dealer net gamma imbalance is at the 12th percentile, and $1.2T of announced buybacks should support. QQQ RSI below 30 has on average led to about a 4% rally over the next five trading days.

Dubravko's AI capex math: every $100B of added capex equals about $9 of 2027 S&P 500 EPS (about 2.5% growth). Capex of about $1.5T would add roughly $18 vs consensus, or 4-5% to 2027 EPS growth. JPM credit analysts expect hyperscalers to fund their 2027 capex absent credit shocks, though funding will need more equity.
Dubravko's catalysts: Middle East developments, megacap IPOs, next month's ERCOT meeting (AI capex implications), and the December Fed meeting.

Mislav says the banks vs staples relative performance has round-tripped to flat on the year. He argues bond yields have peaked and that this will be read as positive, and recommends adding to equities into year-end.

Mislav expects any oil-driven escalation to be short-lived and advises buying dips on escalation. He stays with the broadening call, says AI is not a continued sell, and says Value vs Growth and SPW vs SPX are rebounding with the turn in yields.
Mislav: YTD P/E derating is 10% for MSCI World. He sees the cycle as mid-stage rather than late if ISM and PMIs stay above 50.
CPI is due Nov 10 at 8:30am ET. PPI is due Nov 13. Earnings tomorrow include CRWV, QBTS, RGTI and TDG, and AMAT and CSCO report Nov 12.

sector_views.rationale: Dubravko finds AI Upstream attractive after the positioning flush, and Mislav says AI is not a continued sell. Both see the tech drawdown as an opportunity.
Dubravko sees the best Low Vol opportunity in Healthcare, and the HC desk reports flows leaning about 5x toward buying.
Dubravko says affordability remains a headwind from oil prices, borrowing costs and housing shortages. He sees longer-term value in Apparel, Restaurants and Retail vs Energy.
Dubravko's long 12M momentum vs short 3M momentum idea is essentially Tech vs Energy and Defensives.
Henrici expects a relative breather for renewables if the rest of power trades better, with headline risk from TSLA's solar plant. Democratic policy changes are a positive.

earnings_insights: US earnings Nov 9 included KKR, HIMS, IONS, ROIV, TTD, TTWO, RKLB, OXY, CEG, MARA and LCID. The report gives no figures for these results.
Earnings season was generally very strong, especially for hyperscalers excluding GOOGL Search, per Brian Heavey.
Earnings due Nov 10: CRWV, QBTS, RGTI, TDG, CAPR, INO, LQDA, NN, SGRY and VG. Nov 11: CTVA and VYLR. Nov 12: AMAT, CSCO, TE, FIGR and others. Nov 13: ARI, LXP, PARA and others.
Dubravko estimates about 20% EPS growth in 2027 and a YE26 SPX EPS of $365.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Yields fell on the day. The desk sees peaking yields as a positive for equities.
Oil fell on US/Iran de-escalation headlines. Lower oil eases affordability pressure.
VIX is back near 20 and the desk says the bulk of technical supply may be out of the way.
The next major macro catalyst. The report gives no estimate.
The base case supports the earnings growth estimate of about 20%.

risk_factors: Re-escalation of the US/Iran conflict and oil price spikes.
Low conviction in the bounce, with volumes at YTD lows and the recovery driven by hedge removal and retail buying.
AI Momentum Index has not shown a clear recovery day in 10 days.
NVDA CEO Jensen Huang affair and the lack of a clear successor.
Hyperscaler capex funding mix shifting toward equity, and 2028 data center project concerns after the midterms.
Blue Wave policy may limit the AI capex curve.
Affordability pressure on consumers and the US Government funding deadline on Dec 11.
vol_and_positioning: VIX at 19.92. Dubravko notes dealer net gamma imbalance at the 12th percentile.
Equity L/S net leverage is at 3-year lows, and global momentum exposure is near 3-year lows and close to neutral. The 6m z-score of positioning and price is back near its summer lows.
Momentum crowding reset from the 100th to the 76th percentile. Levered ETFs sold about $60bn last Thursday and $35bn the prior Friday, and exposure is below Jan 2026 levels.
CTAs flipped to net short. Vol targeters' leverage fell from the 65th to the 30th percentile, with about $50bn left to sell.
October Long Momentum fell about 11% (about 6 standard deviations), and Momentum L/S is down about 40% from its peak.
NDX and QQQ RSI at 30. QQQ RSI below 30 has on average preceded about a 4% gain over 5 trading days.
Short interest (JPSIPURE) has stabilized. The AI Momentum Index (JPAIMOPR) kept falling, and the bounce looks driven by hedge removal and retail buying.
geopolitical: Positive US/Iran headlines: apparent agreement on uranium enrichment levels, moving some enriched uranium, and inspections. Trump comments to CNN keep the narrative in de-escalation.
Democrats won new majorities in the House and Senate in last week's midterms. Elizabeth Warren is set to take over the Senate banking committee.
US and China agreed to extend the trade truce through January 20, 2027. The US balks at China's demand for a tightly scripted Trump-Xi-Putin summit.
APEC Leaders Meeting in Shenzhen Nov 18-19, US government funding deadline Dec 11, G20 Summit in Miami Dec 15-16.
